findingsFixed.summary: Tool-only/assistant-only incremental requests incorrectly reset the continuation budget. Only genuine nonempty user input now resets it; injected continue and non-user follow-ups preserve it.

Frozen/non-writable or replaced client hooks could be retained as ready without observing manual user activity. Runtime and verifier now share descriptor-verified wrapper ownership; raw continuation fallback is removed and ownership is rechecked at commit.

Planned dev cleanup used a guessed default marker rather than the actual runtime config root. The ready identity now follows worker/persisted roots/cleanup. Follow-up precision regressions caught native/CIM and Number mismatches; exact FILETIME strings are preserved and checked again against a retained handle at the mutation boundary.

Guidance unnecessarily demanded a full Desktop exit and used the wrong repair-action name. Four real locale resources now prefer in-place repair when a port exists, make managed relaunch conditional, and do not equate prerequisites with delivery.

sourceVerification.scope: Tests and fixtures validate source behavior. They do not prove installed/live behavior. No gate was weakened. The Rust library test build retains three baseline warnings; strict production Clippy passed.

The historical October 25 02:43 Singapore disposable receipt demonstrates a different process/session and directly invoked the guarded bridge. It did not wait for the native 5/10/20-minute scheduler or exercise the dev crash chain.

Request Health checks a reviewed partial Responses structural/replay contract, not all provider semantics or upstream acceptance. Byte-based sizing is approximate diagnostic information, not an exact tokenizer.

Clean/planned exit intentionally does not resume a pending turn. Killing all recovery owners cannot self-relaunch. A restored pending continuation starts a fresh cooldown; its crash ledger can expire after 15 minutes without heartbeat.
